title: Cole Hauser Reveals 'Dutton Ranch' Struggled Without Taylor Sheridan in the Writers' Room
excerpt: The Yellowstone star said 'everything had changed' on the spinoff set as the cast navigated new writers, new directors, and the absence of franchise creator Taylor Sheridan.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Cole Hauser highlighted significant creative challenges on Dutton Ranch without Taylor Sheridan's guidance.
  • Dutton Ranch is the first Yellowstone series not written by Sheridan, led by showrunner Chad Feehan.
  • Co-star Ed Harris nearly quit during Season 1 due to feeling misled about his character's role.
  • Dutton Ranch was renewed for a second season, with production set to begin in early 2027.
  • The franchise faces uncertainty without Sheridan's direct involvement in the creative process.
Creative Challenges on Dutton Ranch
›First series in Yellowstone universe not written by Taylor Sheridan.
›Showrunner Chad Feehan and new writing staff took over.
›Cole Hauser emphasized the need to adapt quickly to new creative dynamics.
›Production faced challenges including extreme Texas temperatures and an ice storm.
https://youtube.com/watch?v=gkUqDg64zB4

Cole Hauser isn't sugarcoating what it took to make Dutton Ranch work. In a candid interview with Film Inside NYC, the actor who has played fan-favorite Rip Wheeler since Yellowstone premiered in 2018 laid bare the difficulties of carrying the franchise forward without its architect, Taylor Sheridan, in the writers' room.

"There were challenges, you know? Not having Taylor there, for us to really kind of be able to work with these new writers, these new directors, these people — everything had changed," Hauser said.

A New Creative Reality

Dutton Ranch, which premiered on Paramount+ in May and wrapped its first season earlier this month, is the first series in the Yellowstone universe that Sheridan did not write. While the 57-year-old franchise creator remained on board as an executive producer, day-to-day creative control shifted to showrunner Chad Feehan and an entirely new writing staff. Entertainment Weekly confirmed in April that Feehan had unexpectedly exited the series ahead of the premiere.

For Hauser, 51, the transition stripped away the creative infrastructure he had relied on for six years across five seasons of Yellowstone. The only familiar faces in the production apparatus were co-star and fellow executive producer Kelly Reilly, actor Finn Little, and director Christina Alexandra Voros.

"It was about putting my head down and working my ass off with what I had around me. We worked our asses off this year."

— Cole Hauser, Actor and Executive Producer, Dutton Ranch

Despite the upheaval, Hauser framed the experience as ultimately rewarding. "We had to figure out on our feet how to really perform and tell a story," he said. "So I'm proud of what we accomplished, and I look forward to doing it again."

Ed Harris Nearly Walked Away

Hauser's remarks follow an even more explosive revelation from co-star Ed Harris, the Oscar-nominated actor who plays Everett McKinney on Dutton Ranch. In an interview with Variety earlier this week, Harris said he came close to leaving the show partway through Season 1.

"I said, 'Get me the f--- out of here,' to tell you the truth. I didn't feel I was being used."

— Ed Harris, Actor, Dutton Ranch

Harris, 75, claimed he was told before signing on that Everett would be one of the show's four main characters. "That wasn't really the case," he told Variety, adding that he felt "a little bit misled" by the scope of the role. He also expressed frustration that a scene in which his character sang was cut from the final edit.

The Golden Globe winner confirmed he will return for Season 2 after producers assured him his character would have a more substantial role. "I'm being told that my character will have a little bit more to do. It just was a little frustrating, to tell you the truth," Harris said.

Ed Harris's Frustration

›Felt misled about his character's prominence in the show.
›Confirmed return for Season 2 with promises of a larger role.
›Expressed frustration over a cut scene featuring his character.

Sheridan's Shifting Empire

Sheridan's reduced involvement in Dutton Ranch reflects a broader pivot in his career. The writer-producer, who built one of television's most lucrative franchises with Yellowstone and spinoffs 1883 and 1923, has reportedly shifted focus. He signed a deal with NBCUniversal last year following reported tensions with Paramount leadership, and has been writing feature film scripts including the action thriller F.A.S.T. and the Call of Duty adaptation.

Kelly Reilly, who plays Beth Dutton alongside Hauser's Rip, offered her own perspective in a press conference ahead of the season finale. "I feel the weight of it," Reilly said. "There is a responsibility. I didn't want to drop the ball. I really wanted to honor the world." She credited her partnership with Hauser as the foundation that held the show together: "We lean on each other. We ask each other advice. We're not doing this on our own."

What's Next for the Franchise

Dutton Ranch was renewed for a second season last month, with production expected to begin in early 2027. The show's first season followed Rip and Beth as they relocated to Rio Paloma, Texas — a stark departure from the Montana landscapes that defined Yellowstone. Filming in Texas brought its own physical challenges, with temperatures hitting 106 degrees Fahrenheit during the first week of production and an ice storm shutting down the set for four days near the end.

What's Next for Dutton Ranch
›Dutton Ranch renewed for a second season.
›Production expected to start in January or February 2027.
›Season 1 followed Rip and Beth's relocation to Texas.
›Filming faced extreme weather challenges, including 106°F heat.

For the millions of Yellowstone fans worldwide — including a substantial following among Indian diaspora audiences who helped make the show a global streaming phenomenon — the behind-the-scenes turmoil raises questions about whether the franchise can sustain its momentum without Sheridan's direct creative hand. Season 2 will be the test.

All episodes of Dutton Ranch Season 1 are currently streaming on Paramount+.
